finding.message: src/presentation/server.ts (presentation) skips layers to import src/persistence/repositories.ts (persistence)

answer.explanation: At lines 12-21, src/presentation/server.ts imports eight concrete repository classes (ApiaryRepository, HiveRepository, HarvestRepository, InspectionRepository, ProductRepository, ScaleRepository, TreatmentRepository, WeightReadingRepository) straight from src/persistence/repositories.ts. At line 22 it also imports TextHiveClient from the persistence layer. The rest of the file works through the business layer: it imports HiveService, ReportService, ScaleService and TreatmentService (lines 2-5) and the business error types (lines 6-11), and createServer takes services as parameters (lines 56-60). The repositories are probably imported so the server module can build and wire the services, acting as a composition root, rather than for request handling. The visible excerpt stops at line 60, so this is not confirmed. Either way, FF-S03 forbids a layer from skipping the layer below it. Here presentation depends directly on persistence instead of going only through business, so the rule flags the edge server.ts:12 -> repositories.ts. The project supplied no docs, ADRs or comments that declare this wiring intentional or that allow presentation to see persistence.

finding.message: src/presentation/server.ts (presentation) skips layers to import src/persistence/textHiveClient.ts (persistence)

answer.explanation: At line 22, src/presentation/server.ts imports `TextHiveClient` straight from the persistence layer (`../persistence/textHiveClient`). FF-S03 flags this because presentation should reach persistence only through the business layer. The same file already does that in other places: it imports `HiveService`, `ReportService`, `ScaleService` and `TreatmentService` from `../business` (lines 2-5), and `createServer` receives those services as parameters (lines 56-60). So the `TextHiveClient` import goes around that service boundary and ties the HTTP layer to a concrete storage client. The file also imports eight repository classes from `../persistence/repositories` (lines 12-21). That suggests either the file also wires up dependencies or the HTTP layer reaches into persistence more widely. The excerpt cuts off before showing how `TextHiveClient` is used, so I can't tell which. I had no project docs, ADRs or comments that address this dependency.
